skills.name: hyperframes
skills.purpose: HeyGen's entry/router skill for making, editing and rendering videos as HTML+GSAP compositions (promos, explainers, captioned clips, title cards, Remotion ports); resumes project state and routes to the right workflow skill.
skills.how_to_use: Triggers on any 'make/edit/render a video' request. Needs Node + the HyperFrames CLI (npx hyperframes) and headless Chrome/ffmpeg for rendering; install with `npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes`.
skills.evidence: Official HeyGen; skills.sh ~737K installs and #2 on skills.sh Hot list (+104 this period); listed in zhuyansen/awesome-claude-video-skills

skills.name: remotion-best-practices
skills.purpose: Official Remotion router skill that loads rules for building videos in React with Remotion (animations, timing, audio, captions, 3D, rendering) and links to the sibling remotion-* skills.
skills.how_to_use: Auto-loads when working in a Remotion project; install with `npx skills add remotion-dev/skills`. Remotion itself needs a company license for teams over 3 people.
skills.evidence: Official Remotion team; skills.sh ~566K installs (most-installed video skill outside HyperFrames); in aitmpl/davila7 templates and many awesome lists
skills.notes: No LICENSE file in repo; Remotion framework has its own source-available license.

skills.name: general-video

skills.how_to_use: Routed from /hyperframes or invoked directly for multi-scene builds; same HyperFrames CLI prerequisites.
skills.evidence: Official HeyGen; skills.sh ~406K installs

skills.name: music-to-video
skills.purpose: Turns a music track (file, video audio, or mood-brief-generated track) into a beat-synced HyperFrames video: lyric video, slideshow or kinetic promo; any supplied images/clips are cut onto the detected beat grid.
skills.how_to_use: Triggers on beat-synced/music-driven video requests; part of the HyperFrames pack (`npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes`); needs Node + HyperFrames CLI.
skills.evidence: Official HeyGen/HyperFrames; skills.sh ~275K installs; also on mcpservers.org. Closest public equivalent to a beat-cut-films workflow.
